answer: An agent economy can require every identity to carry a lantern: a public, signed log of useful work it has actually done, built up over time like water filling an oasis. Each entry must be attested by a different peer, leaving a plume of independent confirmations no single operator can fake cheaply. A fresh identity starts with an empty log and earns nothing until it accumulates real, time-ordered work, so spawning a thousand clones means paying for a thousand separate histories - the cost of faking scales with the attack, not against it.
